newsitem.title: USA: Enova, Pacific Enterprises to merge.
newsitem.headline: Enova, Pacific Enterprises to merge.

text.p: Two California utility companies, Enova Corp. and Pacific Enterprises, said Monday they agreed to a merger that will create the biggest investor-owned utility serving consumers in the United States.

The all-stock merger between Enova, the parent company of San Diego Gas & Electric, and Pacific Enterprises, owner of Southern California Gas Co., will create a company that serves about 6 million customers with a market value of $5.2 billion, the companies said.

Analysts said the merger was part of the already rapid consolidation in the electric and natural gas industries that would put pressure on other utilities in California. Generating and marketing power is gradually being deregulated in the United States.

"Both electricity and gas are being deregulated -- gas companies have been involved with it for several years," said analyst Barry Abramson at Prudential Securities. "As the process continues, the two industries are converging."

Utility mergers boomed in the third quarter, led by Enron Corp.'s $2.1 billion bid for Portland General Corp. Overall, 34 deals worth about $15 billion were announced, making it the second busiest sector behind telecommunications, according to Securities Data Co., a New Jersey company that tracks mergers.

No price was set for the deal announced Monday, under which Pacific Enterprise shareholders will get 1.5038 shares and Enova stockholders one share of the new company for each of the shares they hold.

The companies said they expect the merger to produce cost savings of about $1.2 billion over 10 years, mainly from combining and reducing management and administrative functions. No job cuts or layoffs were cited in their announcement.

Southern California Gas has more than 4.7 million customers in the southern part of the state. San Diego Gas & Electric provides electric service to 1.2 million customers in southern California and gas service to 700,000 customers in San Diego County.
The new company, to be based in San Diego, will have about 60 percent of its revenue from natural gas operations, 35 percent from electricity and the rest from other operations.
It will develop and market new products and services, while customers will continue to do business with San Diego Gas & Electric and Southern California Gas, the companies said in a statement.

Richard Farman, president and chief operating officer of Pacific Enterprises, will become chairman and chief executive of the new company. Stephen Baum, president and chief executive of Enova, will become vice chairman, president and chief operating officer.
Baum will become CEO two years after the effective date of the merger and will add the title of chairman by September 2000, when Farman is to retire, they added.
The board of the new company will include Farman and Baum and have an equal number of outside directors from the two companies.
The new company's dividend is expected to be set at $1.56 a share annually, the dividend currently paid to Enova shareholders, the companies said.
The merger is subject to approval by regulators and shareholders of Enova and Pacific Enterprises. It is expected to close by the end of 1997, the companies said.
Pacific Enterprises stock rose 37.5 cents to $31.875 and Enova was unchanged at $22.50, both in afternoon trading on the New York Stock Exchange.
